short: An early German U-boat that shocked the world by sinking three British armoured cruisers in a single hour.
full:
Commissioned on 18 April 1910, SM U-9 was an early kerosene-powered submarine of the Imperial German Navy. Submarines were still regarded largely as unproven experimental craft by the world's major navies when the First World War began, but U-9 rapidly demonstrated their devastating potential.

On 22 September 1914, under the command of Otto Weddigen, U-9 encountered a patrol of three British Cressy-class armoured cruisers in the North Sea. In less than an hour, she torpedoed and sank all three — HMS Aboukir, HMS Hogue, and HMS Cressy — killing nearly 1,500 British sailors. This single action fundamentally altered naval strategy, proving that the submarine was a deadly weapon capable of challenging surface superiority. U-9 survived the war and surrendered to the British in November 1918.
